Pinhitch — map-first community interface

The idea

Local problems are easier to solve together.

People often face the same problems in their neighbourhood without knowing that others are dealing with them too.

Pinhitch puts those problems on a map. People can post a problem at a location, discover nearby issues, show support with “Me Too”, add updates, discuss the problem, and work toward resolution.

What I built

A community product built around place.

01

Map-first discovery

An interactive map for nearby problem discovery, categories, place search, geolocation, and map-linked state.

02

Realtime community

Supabase realtime keeps problems and community activity reflected in the interface without manual refreshes.

03

Resolution workflow

Problems move through structured updates such as in progress, ETA, escalated, and resolved, with community confirmation.

Engineering

More than a frontend.

Pinhitch combines an Astro shell with React for interactive application areas. Supabase provides authentication, Postgres, PostGIS, and realtime subscriptions.

Geospatial discovery

PostGIS handles nearby discovery using geographical distance queries, making location part of the application data model rather than just a visual map layer.

Realtime state

Supabase subscriptions keep the interface synchronized as problems and community activity change, while optimistic interactions keep common actions feeling immediate.

Privacy by design

Personal problems can use fuzzy locations so users can participate without exposing their exact location to other people.

Responsive interaction

Desktop detail panels become draggable mobile bottom sheets, keeping the map useful while preserving access to the details.

Architecture

Keeping the UI separate from the data layer.

Database access lives in domain-level query modules instead of being scattered through components. That keeps product UI, application logic, and persistence easier to reason about.

Application flow

Reflection

Building the product was only part of the problem.

Pinhitch pushed me beyond frontend implementation into product architecture, geospatial data modelling, realtime systems, and privacy considerations.

The biggest lesson was that data freshness, privacy, mobile interaction, discoverability, and network density all become part of the engineering problem when the product depends on people and place.
